cohort: 170,121 women in Slovenia who delivered singleton pregnancies at or after 38 weeks' gestation between 2003 and 2012.
finding: Cesarean section rates, both urgent and elective, increase with increasing BMI, irrespective of weight gain pattern.
mod_finding: The frequency of urgent cesareans increases in all women and the frequency of elective cesareans among obese women decreases as the level of weight gain increases from undergainers to overgainers.
